text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your skin condition, can you tell me how long these lesions have been present and have they changed in appearance or number since they first appeared?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the recent exposure to chickenpox and the up-to-date immunization status, I need to determine if this is a modified presentation. Do the lesions appear to be in different stages of healing, or are they all at the same stage of development?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: These pearly, umbilicated papules are classic for Molluscum contagiosum, a common viral skin infection in children. To confirm the diagnosis, I will examine the lesions more closely. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Previously healthy, up-to-date immunizations, no significant illnesses. Social history: Attends daycare three times per week.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of skin-colored, pearly papules with central umbilication is pathognomonic for Molluscum contagiosum, caused by a poxvirus. Given the classic morphology and exposure history, I am confident in the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
